memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "'But if just one person sins unintentionally, that person must bring a year-old female goat for a sin offering. The priest is to make atonement before the Lord for the one who erred by sinning unintentionally, and when atonement has been made for that person, they will be forgiven.'" — Num 15:27-28 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Having provided for the sins of the whole community, God now turns to the individual: "if just one person sins unintentionally." He does not deal only with the crowd; He cares about each single soul. Even one person's wrong is worth His attention and His provision for atonement.

There is great tenderness in this. It would be easy to think that God, ruling over a nation of hundreds of thousands, might only concern Himself with the big picture. But no — He makes careful provision for the one. The individual matters to God. Your sins, your need for forgiveness, your standing before Him — He does not overlook you in the crowd.

This reflects the heart of God throughout Scripture. He is the Shepherd who leaves the ninety-nine to seek the one. He knows each of His people by name. You are never lost in the mass to Him. When you come to Him with your own particular failures, He receives you personally and individually.

And again the promise rings out: "they will be forgiven." Whether it is a whole community or a single struggling soul, the outcome of God's appointed atonement is the same — forgiveness, full and free. In Christ, this personal mercy is ours. He did not die merely for humanity in the abstract, but for you, by name. As Paul marvelled, the Son of God "loved me and gave himself for me." Bring your own sins to Him, and know that His mercy is personal.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do you ever feel lost in the crowd, as if God overlooks you?
2. How does God's provision for the individual reassure you?
3. What does it mean to you that Christ "loved me and gave himself for me"?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, thank You that I am never lost in the crowd to You. You see me, know me by name, and provide forgiveness for me personally in Christ. Thank You that Jesus loved me and gave Himself for me. Amen.
